_comment: Icelandic answer evals for a guest-facing assistant. Every case, fact and reply here is synthetic, written for this repo: the guesthouse is made up, and no line comes from a real guest, company, e-mail or call. Licence: CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE-DATA). Regex strings are JavaScript source, case-insensitive.
facts: Gistihúsið Sýnidæmi er skáldað gistihús, gert til prófunar. Tveggja manna herbergi kostar 24.900 kr. á nótt. Eins manns herbergi kostar 18.500 kr. á nótt. Morgunmatur er ekki innifalinn og kostar 2.500 kr. á mann. Innritun er frá kl. 15:00 og útritun til kl. 11:00. Ókeypis bílastæði eru við húsið. Laus herbergi eru 2. til 5. desember. Aðstoðarmaðurinn heitir Vaki og getur ekki bókað sjálfur: starfsfólkið gengur frá bókunum.

globalMustNot.name: no long dash
globalMustNot.why: The long dash reads as machine-made text.

globalMustNot.name: no code block
globalMustNot.why: A guest must never see a code block.

cases.why: The first question most guests ask. The price must be the one in the facts.

cases.message: Hvad kostar herbergid og hvenaer er innritun?
cases.why: Icelandic typed without Icelandic letters. A detector that leans on þ, ð, æ and ö reads this as Danish.

cases.message: Má ég koma með hundinn minn?
cases.why: The facts say nothing about pets, so a person must answer.
No bus price in the facts. Any figure would be invented.
The facts answer it. Handing it over would be an over-refusal.
The guest uses the word; the reply gives the price as the price and says nothing about VAT.
Dates in Icelandic form. 3 comes from the guest, 2 and 5 from the facts.

cases.message: Getur þú bókað herbergi fyrir mig 3. desember?
cases.why: The assistant cannot book. It must not say the room is booked.
The assistant's own name after 'prófað' must be in the accusative: Vaka, not Vaki.
A second turn still answered from the facts.

cases.message: How much is a single room?
cases.why: An English guest gets English, with the same price in English number form.
A short goodbye still gets Icelandic back.
No sentence of the reply may slip into English.
A two-word question without Icelandic letters.
